LESSON: CONSTRUCTING WATER RETENTION STRUCTURES

Grade: Grade 7
Subject: AGRICULTURE
Strand: Conservation of Resources
Topic 1.2: Constructing Water Retention Structures

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Constructing Water Retention Structures. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How can surface run-off be conserved for gardening purposes?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. describe how surface run-off can be used in gardening
2. construct water retention structures to conserve surface runoff

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: CONSTRUCTING WATER RETENTION STRUCTURES
Subject: AGRICULTURE · Grade: Grade 7
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Constructing Water Retention Structures helps you succeed in AGRICULTURE. You will understand it, practise it, and use it in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

KEY FACTS ABOUT WATER
We use water for drinking, cooking, cleaning, and farming.
Conserve water: close taps, fix leaks, reuse grey water for plants where safe.
Unsafe water can cause disease — store drinking water in clean covered containers.

PART 1: Describe how surface run-off can be used in gardening

What this means
In this part you learn to describe how surface run-off can be used in gardening. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: describe how surface run-off can be used in gardening.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Observe: Name what you can see/touch about “Constructing Water Retention Structures” around your school.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can describe how surface run-off can be used in gardening. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Construct water retention structures to conserve surface runoff

What this means
In this part you learn to construct water retention structures to conserve surface runoff. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: construct water retention structures to conserve surface runoff.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Explain: Say why Constructing Water Retention Structures matters for health, safety, or the environment in Kenya.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can construct water retention structures to conserve surface runoff. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Constructing Water Retention Structures is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Conserve water: close taps, fix leaks, reuse grey water for plants where safe.

Example 1: Name what you can see/touch about “Constructing Water Retention Structures” around your school. (skill: describe how surface run-off can be used in gardening)

Example 2: Say why Constructing Water Retention Structures matters for health, safety, or the environment in Kenya. (skill: construct water retention structures to conserve surface runoff)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Constructing Water Retention Structures to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: describe how surface run-off can be used in gardening.
3. Practise this skill: construct water retention structures to conserve surface runoff.
4. Make one local Kenya example of Constructing Water Retention Structures from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Constructing Water Retention Structures: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 7 learner study Constructing Water Retention Structures?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How can surface run-off be conserved for gardening purposes?
2. How does the construction of water retention structures conserve water?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Constructing Water Retention Structures means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: describe how surface run-off can be used in gardening.
5. Be able to: construct water retention structures to conserve surface runoff.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
